t.E472e.agn: In 2020 EFSA set an ADI based on the group ADI of 240 mg/kg body weight, expressed as tartaric acid, and found no safety concern at the reported use levels. In its 2025 follow-up opinion EFSA cited an ADI of 600 mg/kg body weight for this additive and stated that estimated intake remained below this value.
t.E472e.body: During digestion in the body it is largely broken down into glycerol, fatty acids and the corresponding organic acids (acetic and/or tartaric acid); these are used like the fats in foods.
t.E472e.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E472e.prod: It is an emulsifier produced from vegetable or animal fats by a chemical reaction (esterification).
t.E472e.regx.0: Re-evaluated; ADI set based on the tartaric acid group ADI (240 mg/kg body weight per day), no safety concern.
t.E472e.regx.1: Follow-up opinion: ADI of 600 mg/kg body weight per day; estimated intake below the ADI. A change to the specifications recommended.
t.E472e.summary: An emulsifier (DATEM) derived from mono- and diglycerides. It strengthens bread dough and increases its volume.
t.E472e.what: It strengthens dough and increases volume in bread; used as an emulsifier.
